  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a sourced B2B payer with real budget. Paid competitors publish per-agent or per-team pricing: CrankWheel Solo at $29/mo and Team from $99/mo, and Blitzz from about $15-45/agent/mo. One customer at that price matters within 90 days. Idea B's sourced pricing sits at $0.05-$0.10/min or $3-5/mo, so a single customer barely registers.",
    "Idea A names a plausible underserved segment the evidence supports: small 5-20 agent teams poorly served by enterprise 'talk to sales' motions. Idea B's own case-against concedes at least four near-identical pay-per-minute competitors, which leaves no stated differentiation.",
    "Idea B's market is squeezed from below by sourced free or one-time alternatives (MacWhisper lifetime purchase). Idea B's own seed HN thread shows the poster adopting MacWhisper rather than paying per minute. That undercuts willingness to pay for the proposed product.",
    "Idea B's acquisition math looks poor from its own sources. App-store CPI of under $1 to over $15 is set against revenue measured in cents per minute. Idea A's Zendesk Marketplace channel reaches buyers already budgeting $500-$5,000+/year for add-ons.",
    "Idea A has real weaknesses: its demand quotes come from family caregivers rather than support teams, it competes with free tools (Quick Assist, JoinByKey), and compliance expectations (SOC 2, HIPAA) may gate deals. Even so, its payer evidence is stronger than anything in Idea B."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand quotes don't show demand for a standalone cheap transcription tool. They complain that bundled products are expensive: Notion AI in the r/automation thread and Ultimate Brain in the r/selfpublish thread. The seed HN thread resolves with the poster adopting MacWhisper, a one-time-purchase competitor. Separately, the case-against claims about Google's free transcription app and Untold's free bundling carry no URLs, so they count as unsourced.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Neither brief has demand evidence from the actual intended payer. Idea A's quotes come from consumers helping parents, not support managers. Idea A also carries compliance and free-competitor risk that could stall a first B2B deal within 90 days. Idea A wins mainly because Idea B's evidence actively argues against its viability, not because Idea A is strongly validated."
}
